headline: New law requires the federal health department to create and update a national plan to prevent, treat, and cure Parkinson's disease.
what_it_does: The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) must run a project on Parkinson's disease and related conditions, including a national plan to guide efforts to prevent, diagnose, treat, and cure it and to improve patient care. HHS must update the plan over time and assess each year how prepared the country is for the growing number of people with the disease. The law also creates an advisory council of federal and non-federal members to make recommendations to HHS. These requirements end after 2035.

who_it_affects.group: People with Parkinson's disease and related conditions
who_it_affects.how: Federal efforts to research, diagnose, treat, and improve care for their condition will be coordinated under a national plan.

who_it_affects.group: Families and caregivers of people with Parkinson's
who_it_affects.how: The national plan includes efforts to improve care for people living with the disease.

who_it_affects.group: Department of Health and Human Services
who_it_affects.how: The agency must create, carry out, and update the plan, do yearly assessments, and work with a new advisory council.
Non-federal stakeholders can serve on the new advisory council that makes recommendations on prevention and treatment.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted July 2, 2024; provisions end at the close of 2035.
